Research

Decoding Opioid Neuroinflammation
at the Molecular Level

NIH Grant R01 DA51875 — first systematic characterization of KATP ion channel expression and functional activity in human macrophage-lineage cells across polarization states under chronic opioid exposure.

M.S. Thesis — NIH R01 DA51875 — Klein Lab, University at Buffalo

KATP Channels in Microglia: A New Lens on Opioid Neuroinflammation

Using THP-1-derived macrophages differentiated into M0, M1, and M2 phenotypes, I established that KATP subunits (KCNJ8, ABCC8, ABCC9) are stably expressed across all polarization states and that functional channel activity is phenotype-dependent, mirroring each state's metabolic program. Basal potassium flux follows M0 > M2 > M1, consistent with glycolytic high-ATP in M1 cells holding channels closed. Chronic morphine produced dose- and phenotype-specific flux shifts without altering mRNA, implicating post-translational regulation as the key opioid mechanism.

4KATP Subunits
3Phenotypes
11Figures
65+References
Key Findings

What We Discovered

  • KCNJ8, ABCC8, ABCC9 stably expressed across all polarization states — confirming KATP relevance in immune cells.
  • M2 macrophages respond selectively to pinacidil (SUR2 agonist), suggesting preferential Kir6.1/SUR2 membrane availability in oxidative-phosphorylation-dependent cells.
  • Diazoxide at 100 µM suggests mitochondrial KATP activation — a mechanistically distinct finding in immune biology.
  • Morphine modulates KATP functional activity without changing mRNA — implicating post-translational regulation.
  • Confocal live-cell imaging corroborated plate-reader findings with M2 showing greatest cumulative thallium flux.
Why It Matters

Broader Significance

Over 80,000 Americans die from opioid overdoses annually. This work identifies microglial KATP channels as candidate drug targets, provides mechanistic rationale for KATP agonists as opioid therapy adjuncts, establishes a validated human cell platform for neuroimmune KATP studies, and lays translational groundwork for primary microglia and in vivo validation.

Experimental Platform

Multi-Modal Methodology

  • THP-1 differentiation: PMA + LPS/IFN-γ (M1) or IL-4/IL-13 (M2), 72h; 6-, 24-, 96-, 384-well formats
  • RT-qPCR: SYBR Green, BioRad CFX; 6-point standard curve; GAPDH normalized; n=12
  • Thallium flux: BioTek Synergy H1; 96-well; n=5; diazoxide & pinacidil pharmacological probes
  • Confocal live-cell imaging: Leica DMi8/TCS SP8; xyt time-lapse; Fiji ROI analysis
  • Stats: One/two-way ANOVA (Prism), three-way ANOVA + linear mixed-effects model (SPSS)
  • In-vitro electrophysiology exposure (NaNion platform); in-vivo shadowing: von Frey, glucose tolerance testing

Academic Projects

Research Projects

M.S. Thesis Project

AUG 2024 — MAY 2026 · Klein Lab, UB

Modeling Microglia Expression and Function of KATP Channels During Chronic Opioid Exposure in an In-Vitro Cell Model

Differentiated THP-1 human monocytic leukemia cells into M0, M1, and M2 microglial phenotypes and validated the in-vitro model. Investigated the role of KATP channels under normal and chronic opioid conditions to understand functional changes in neurodegeneration and chronic pain. Compared findings across multi-platform molecular, functional, and imaging assays.

B.Pharm Thesis

JAN 2024 — JUN 2024 · Dr. Vidhu Aeri's Lab · Team of 3

Comparative Pharmacognostic Evaluation of Adhatoda vasica, Adenanthera pavonina, and Ailanthus excelsa

Carried out morphological study, powder microscopy, and TLC fingerprint profiling of three medicinal plants and their mixtures. Generated pharmacopoeia-benchmarked comparative datasets and submitted full thesis with committee defense.
